title: Sprint sift — Console intake & prioritization playbook (Sept 2026)
content:
Sprint Sift — Console Intake & Prioritization Playbook (Sept 2026)

Purpose
  - Provide a lightweight, repeatable funnel for intake -> triage -> sprint-slice decisions for Console & Rollouts work.
  - Make explicit tradeoffs (customer impact vs. dev effort vs. infra/risk) so product and eng agree on what to cut or defer during tight sprints.

Scope
  - Applies to new features, visibility requests, and operational tooling changes tied to the Redwood Console (Rollouts, Routing, Observability panels).
  - Does NOT include infra-only SRE tickets or large Dedicated/Private deployment contracts (those follow separate roadmap gating).

Intake funnel (quick reference)
  1) Intake form submitted -> Slack triage channel + automatic tag in Jira (console-intake).
  2) Triage owner (rotating by week) marks preliminary category: bug | UX | feature | ops | compliance.
  3) Gather 3 anchors: customer (who asked), business outcome (OKR link if any), proposed MVE.
  4) Quick scoring (5–10 min): apply Triage Rubric below.
  5) Outcome: Candidate for next sprint | Backlog deferred | Needs research spike | Escalate to roadmap review.

Triage rubric (score 0-10 per axis, apply weights)
  - Customer impact (weight 3): number of customers affected + strategic importance.
  - Frequency / surface area (weight 2): how often users hit this flow.
  - SLO / reliability risk (weight 2): could this cause outages or latency regressions?
  - Developer effort (weight -2): estimated story points (higher effort lowers score).
  - Infra cost / unit economics (weight -1): changes that materially increase per-token cost.
  - Security/compliance (weight 3): regulatory blockers force prioritization.
  - UX clarity / conversion (weight 1): measurable product metric upside.
  - Regression risk (weight -1): changes that may cause downstream regressions across deployments.

Scoring rules (quick formula)
  - Raw = sum(axis_score * axis_weight). Normalize to a 0-100 scale.
  - Decision thresholds: >= 60 fast-track; 40-59 candidate; < 40 defer unless escalated.

Decision heuristics (policy shortcuts)
  - Any item with Security/compliance >= 8 -> mandatory (skip normal defer).
  - Bugs causing SLO breaches -> immediate triage into current sprint (severity 1).
  - Customer-paid enterprise ask with signed contract -> bump priority + assign customer-success reviewer.
  - UX tweaks with low effort (<= 3 SP) and measurable conversion -> greenlight for next sprint.

Prioritized intake (current snapshot, Sept 2026 grooming)
  - RED-2378 | rollout-visibility-filter | Score 78 | Reason: multiple enterprise customers requesting better per-route filtering for rollouts; medium effort (8 SP); infra risk low; owner: Liam. Planned sprint: 26. Acceptance: filter persisted per-tenant, server-side pagination.
  - RED-2419 | route-decision-surface | Score 64 | Reason: ties into smart-routing pilot; high product value but larger infra coord (12 SP). Plan: spike in 26, feature in 27.
  - RED-2451 | audit-log-export | Score 59 | Reason: compliance ask from two regulated customers; work involves export format and KMS checks (6 SP). Plan: canary in 26 with limited export rows.
  - RED-2509 | console-search-fuzzy | Score 48 | Reason: improves dev velocity; low infra cost but unknown UX lift; effort 5 SP. Plan: test A/B in 26.
  - RED-2530 | rollout-undo-button | Score 34 | Reason: nice-to-have safety feature; medium effort 6 SP; lower immediate impact. Defer to backlog unless championed by customer.
  - RED-2566 | route-cost-estimator | Score 32 | Reason: complex infra impact on per-token accounting; high engineering effort (15 SP). Action: scope into two spikes or drop.
  - RED-2604 | onboard-checklist-redwood | Score 27 | Reason: internal onboarding UX; low external impact; small effort 3 SP. Candidate for sprint slack-fill.
  - RED-2632 | rollout-traffic-simulator | Score 21 | Reason: research-heavy, high infra cost. Backlog.

Wireframe and low-fi notes
  - Reference frames in Figma: figma.com/file/abcdef/Console-Intake-Frames (frames: Intake-01, Rollout-Filters-03, AuditExport-02).
  - Rollout visibility filter: inline pill-based filter, default saved view per org, multi-select with server-side pagination. Keyboard nav required for power users.
  - Audit export modal: two-step (select scope -> confirm KMS policy). Keep modal microcopy minimal.
  - Route decision surface: inline hinting for policy fallback and live cost delta preview (estimated cents per 1k tokens).

Wireframe sketch (ascii micro-layout for Rollout filters)
  - [Search box] [Saved view dropdown v] [Pill: env:prod] [Pill: region:us-west] [Add filter +] [Apply] 
  - Each pill has small caret to expose advanced options (regex, negate).

Rollout of decisions & observability
  - Canary plan for changes touching routing/rollouts: staged across 3 segments (internal -> pilot customers -> GA). Use feature flags and traffic mirroring where possible.
  - Metrics to watch during canary: error rate by tenant, 90th latency for serve endpoints, token-cost delta, rollback events.

Meeting notes (sprint grooming 2026-09-07)
  - Attendees: Priya (product), Liam (eng), Sofia (design), Ethan (SRE).
  - Consensus: fast-track RED-2378 (filters) and RED-2419 spike. Defer rollout-simulator. Split route-cost-estimator into cost-model spike + UI stub.
  - Open question: do we need dedicated telemetry to track per-filter evaluation latency? SRE to scope.

Actionable next steps
  - Priya: update RED-2378 acceptance criteria with persisted-saved-views example JSON (due 2026-09-09).
  - Liam: schedule spike for RED-2419 and assign engineer (due 2026-09-10).
  - Sofia: create hi-fi mock of filter pill interactions and keyboard flows (due 2026-09-11).
  - Ethan: draft telemetry plan for per-filter latency and token-cost delta (due 2026-09-13).

Open questions / flags
  - Enterprise customers asked for per-route RBAC; is this a tech debt item or new feature? (Flagged to Security & Compliance).
  - Is the per-token cost preview feasible without significant extra compute on the critical path? Engineering to quantify.

Appendix: quick scoring cheat sheet
  - Customer impact scale: 0 (none) | 5 (single team) | 8 (multiple customers) | 10 ( enterprise contract affected).
  - Effort mapping: 1-3 small, 4-8 medium, 9+ large. Use story points from last 3 sprints to calibrate.

Notes to reviewer
  - This is meant to be a lightweight working doc for the next two grooming cycles. If you see a ticket that should be escalated, add a short justification comment in the Jira ticket and mention in #console-triage.

Document history
  - 2026-09-05 created (initial intake funnel + rubric).
  - 2026-09-07 grooming meeting notes appended.
  - 2026-09-08 updated prioritized snapshot after stakeholder sync.
